Encore 0.6.0: nothing to set up. Encore now finds a song's audio on its own,
with no Python, Deno or yt-dlp to download.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.6.0_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.6.0_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.6.0_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.6.0_amd64.AppImage` |

Encore 0.5 updates itself to this version: it downloads it in the background
and installs it the next time you quit, or right away with **Restart to
update**. Updating keeps your session, settings and downloads. From 0.4 or
earlier, download it from this page.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** a fresh download asks you to choose **Open Anyway** in **System
  Settings → Privacy & Security** once. After an update, macOS asks once
  again for access to your saved session in the Keychain; choose **Always
  Allow**.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.

## What's new

- **Nothing to set up.** Encore used to download yt-dlp and the Python and
  Deno it runs on before it could play anything. It now finds a song's audio
  itself, with an extractor that follows yt-dlp's and yt-dlp's own challenge
  solver built into the app. The setup screen is gone.
- **120 to 160 MB back.** The first launch of 0.6.0 removes the player
  components 0.5 downloaded. Nothing else in Encore's folders is touched.
- **Clearer reasons.** When a song can't play, Encore says why: a bot check,
  a song that isn't available in your country, an age restriction, a private
  or removed video, a live stream. When YouTube changes something only a
  newer Encore can follow, the message and **Settings → Playback** say so.
- Some songs wait a few seconds before they start, as long as YouTube holds
  them back for an ad. Encore now says so instead of looking stuck.
- **Show all** opens a grid with **Find**, a sort (newest, oldest, A to Z)
  and filters for albums, singles and EPs.
- Long album, playlist and artist descriptions fold to three lines, with
  **More** and **Less**, and YouTube's Wikipedia credit becomes a short line
  with links. Very long playlist titles stop at three lines.
- **Settings → Playback → Player engine** shows what Encore plays with, and
  can reset its player cache.

## Fixes

- **Linux:** the AppImage could close at start on newer systems (seen on
  Fedora 44): it now turns off the WebKit renderer that crashed there.
- Signed out, Encore sent no visitor id to YouTube Music, because YouTube's
  visitor ids grew longer than Encore accepted.
- Cookies YouTube sets with its usual expiry date format were dropped as if
  they had expired.
- Downloads take their loudness from the same request that finds the song,
  so a new download needs one request less.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
